stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
The model is optimized for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image support.

stories.title: SpaceX declares Starship ready for orbit, sets launch date next week
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: SpaceX has announced that its Starship vehicle is prepared for an orbital flight test.
Achieving orbit is highlighted as a major, significant milestone for the program.
A specific launch date for the test is scheduled for the upcoming week.

stories.title: Agility’s new humanoid robot will stop, squat to avoid harming human coworkers
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Agility is developing a humanoid robot designed for collaborative human environments.
The robot incorporates advanced safety features, such as stopping and squatting to prevent harm to coworkers.
This development signals a shift toward deploying robots outside of traditional, caged industrial settings.

stories.title: Corrupt Plans, Clean Traces: Evading Chain-of-Thought Monitoring with Plan Injection
stories.author: Vasilis Syrgkanis
bullet_points: Introduces 'plan injection,' a novel adversarial attack against Chain-of-Thought (CoT) monitoring systems.
The attack involves injecting seemingly benign but harmful reasoning into an LLM's context to bypass safety monitors.
This research highlights a critical vulnerability in current LLM safety strategies designed to detect unsafe planning.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the core field of large language models (LLMs) and text generation.
The associated tags indicate its use within the Hugging Face ecosystem, involving transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under key AI/ML tags including 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's latest large language models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for autonomous agents.
The model is designed for multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes major investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly gaining traction, serving 8.9 million developers in the open models space.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance using Gemma 4 saw up to a 90% speed increase on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using its MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes local-first operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Meta’s new One subscriptions put a price on social media and AI
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Meta is introducing 'Meta One' subscription bundles to monetize its ecosystem.
These bundles pair existing standalone app subscriptions with enhanced AI usage via Muse.
The tiered offerings are available globally for individual users, creators, and businesses.

stories.title: The Router Within: Eliciting Native Skill Routing from a Frozen LLM
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Proposes a novel method to achieve native skill routing within a frozen Large Language Model (LLM) without relying on external context loading.
Argues that the routing signal for selecting appropriate skills is inherently present within the LLM's own forward passes.
Demonstrates that two linear maps are sufficient to effectively 'read' and utilize this internal routing signal, bypassing limitations of context window size.

stories.title: PaperDoctor: Evidence-Grounded and Actionable Feedback for Scientific Papers in Progress
stories.author: James Zou
bullet_points: Introduces PaperDoctor, an agent framework designed to provide evidence-grounded and actionable feedback on scientific papers before submission.
Addresses the scalability issue of human peer review by automating the diagnostic assessment of research drafts.
Focuses on mitigating the risk of flawed claims entering the scientific literature due to the rise of autoresearch agents.

stories.title: We got admin access to Baseten's production GitHub in 25 minutes
stories.author: bearsyankees
bullet_points: A security breach occurred where an attacker gained admin access to Baseten's production GitHub repository.
The compromise was achieved rapidly, reportedly within 25 minutes.
This highlights critical vulnerabilities in software supply chain security and access controls.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weights model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: AI and data centers are incredibly unpopular in every poll
stories.author: Richard Lawler
bullet_points: New poll data indicates significant public unpopularity regarding AI and data center construction.
61% of surveyed likely voters oppose the building of data centers needed to power AI technology.
The findings align with existing political trends and public sentiment regarding AI infrastructure.

stories.title: Microsoft announces Windows and Surface event for October 7th
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is hosting a major Windows and Surface event on October 7th in San Francisco.
The event is positioned to outline the future direction of Windows and Surface devices.
A key focus of the announcement will be the role of local AI in shaping the next chapter of the operating system.

stories.title: The Roman telescope has enough gas for 22 years, double NASA's expectations
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: The Roman Space Telescope is pioneering in-space refueling technology.
The current fuel supply is projected to last for 22 years, exceeding initial NASA estimates.
This capability marks a significant advancement for long-duration space missions.

stories.title: Boston dumps Flock, says it shared data nationwide in violation of contract
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: Boston city government is taking action against Flock, a technology provider.
The core issue is that Flock allegedly enabled 'nationwide lookup' functionality.
This functionality reportedly violated the terms of the contract signed with the city.

stories.title: Demand for EV chargers is outstripping supply, says ChargePoint report
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: EV adoption is increasing in the US market.
The demand for electric vehicle charging infrastructure is currently exceeding available supply.
A ChargePoint report highlights the growing bottleneck in charging availability relative to EV growth.

stories.title: Stellar Colosseum: A Many-Agent Harness for Long-Horizon Research in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science
stories.author: Vahab Mirrokni
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of current LLMs in handling long-horizon, sequential research problems in math and theoretical CS.
Introduces 'Stellar Colosseum,' a model-agnostic harness designed to manage and allocate inference across complex research paths.
Features mechanisms like exploring alternative strategies and a 'readiness gate' to guide the decomposition of difficult proofs.

stories.title: Vulnerability Localization Benchmark: Measuring Agentic Security Analysis at Repository Scale
stories.author: Amin Karbasi
bullet_points: Introduces the Vulnerability Localization Benchmark (VLoc Bench) to address a gap in current security evaluations.
Focuses on 'vulnerability localization'—identifying the specific code files responsible for a weakness within a large repository.
Addresses the growing trend of language-model agents operating over entire software codebases.

stories.title: SlipSense: Multimodal Tactile Learning for Low-Latency and Generalized Slip Detection
stories.author: Tao Yu
bullet_points: Introduces SlipSense, a multimodal framework for low-latency and generalized slip detection in dexterous manipulation.
Utilizes a compact sensor (TacV5) combining a $32 	imes 32$ piezoresistive array (240 Hz) and a 3-axis MEMS accelerometer (8 kHz).
Addresses limitations in existing systems regarding precise latency characterization and cross-platform generalization.

stories.title: Privacy-enhanced federated learning via asynchronous aggregation and local differential perturbation
stories.author: Liesheng Wei
bullet_points: Proposes a privacy-enhanced federated learning framework for secure distributed training.
Integrates Dynamic Differential Privacy (DDP), Homomorphic Encryption (HE), and Local Differential Privacy (LDP) for data protection.
Utilizes an asynchronous aggregation strategy with version control to support distributed environments.

stories.title: Intrinsic Robot Rewarding: Reusing VLA Representations for Autonomous Evaluation and Policy Improvement
stories.author: Elham Al-Fuqara
bullet_points: Introduces 'Intrinsic Robot Rewarding' (IRR) to enhance robot learning.
IRR leverages existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) system representations for self-evaluation.
The method uses successful demonstration endpoints as task-specific references to guide policy improvement.

stories.title: Neuro-Symbolic Hierarchical Intention Anticipation in Human Behavior
stories.author: Ghazaleh Khodabandelou
bullet_points: Proposes a framework for autonomous systems to anticipate human goals before observed behavior is finished.
Frames anticipation as goal inference from multimodal data, moving beyond simple motor forecasting.
Introduces a Hierarchical Planning Decoder (HPD) integrated with a neuro-symbolic encoder for multi-level prediction.

stories.title: Distributed JEPA: A Self-Supervised Framework for Energy Forecasting
stories.author: Elissaios Sarmas
bullet_points: Proposes a Distributed Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) for energy forecasting.
Addresses limitations of traditional methods by using self-supervised learning on heterogeneous energy time-series.
Aims to improve transferability and capture general temporal dynamics across different energy assets.

stories.title: CLARE: Scalable Class-Incremental Continual Learning via a Sparsity-Based Framework
stories.author: Yizhou Yu
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, where models fail to retain old knowledge while learning new tasks.
The proposed method, CLARE, introduces a sparsity-based framework to improve scalability in sequential, multi-task learning scenarios.
It aims to overcome performance degradation caused by inter-task interference and loss of plasticity in existing continual learning models.

stories.title: An Empirical Study of Counterfactual Self-Explanations in LLMs
stories.author: Giorgos Stamou
bullet_points: The study investigates the faithfulness of self-explanations generated by Large Language Models (LLMs).
It uses counterfactual explanations—minimally altering input to change the model's prediction—to test these explanations.
The research evaluates ten instruction-tuned models from LLaMA-3 and Qwen-2.5 families across sentiment analysis and NLI tasks.

stories.title: Shared-Prefix KV Reuse Across Standard LoRA Adapters: Quality and Serving Tradeoffs
stories.author: Dushyant Rajput
bullet_points: Investigates the practical trade-offs of reusing the Key-Value (KV) cache from a shared backbone across multiple LoRA specialists.
Focuses on assessing the impact on task quality when implementing this KV cache reuse for already-trained standard LoRA adapters.
Quantifies the potential serving cost savings achieved by this shared KV cache strategy in multi-specialist deployment scenarios.

stories.title: Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations
stories.author: Ruifeng Xu
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in current LLM-based conversational agents regarding long-term memory.
Existing methods rely on static heuristics, failing to adapt memory management to evolving user needs.
A new framework, ICML (Interactive Memory Learning), is proposed to enable adaptive and self-evolving memory.

stories.title: EviScope: Paired Counterfactual Evidence Diagnostics for Faithful and Efficient Grounded Language Models
stories.author: Suryadeep Singh Deswal
bullet_points: Introduces EviScope, a new benchmark designed to evaluate grounded language models beyond simple final answer accuracy.
EviScope uses paired counterfactual evidence diagnostics by systematically altering the supporting evidence (adding, removing, contradicting it).
The benchmark provides fine-grained evaluation by including span-level support labels for automated assessment.

stories.title: Diagnosing the Fact-Grounding Gap in Multi-Hop Question Answering
stories.author: Richard Zhu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the 'Fact-Grounding Gap' in Multi-Hop Question Answering (QA) systems.
It investigates the source of errors in complex QA, moving beyond simple document retrieval failures.
Failures are decomposed into two distinct modes: retrieval failures and errors occurring at individual reasoning steps.

stories.title: ThinkFlow: Self-Evolving Probabilistic Latent Memory for Lifelong Conversational Agents
stories.author: Ruifeng Xu
bullet_points: Introduces 'ThinkFlow,' a novel self-evolving probabilistic latent memory system for conversational AI.
Addresses the limitations of current explicit textual memory pipelines, which suffer from information bottlenecks and static nature.
Aims to enable lifelong conversational agents to autonomously adapt to user habits by mimicking human cognitive modeling.

stories.title: Can LLMs Follow the Pulse of a Crisis? Evaluating Crisis Sentiment in Bangladesh's July Uprising
stories.author: Mohammad Ali Moni
bullet_points: Introduces UNRESTSENT200K, a new dataset of ~200K Bangla social media comments related to the Bangladesh uprising.
Addresses the challenge of crisis sentiment analysis in low-resource languages like Bangla, where context changes rapidly.
The dataset is structured across five distinct phases of the crisis, from escalation to regime transition.

stories.title: The Role of Implicit and Explicit Demographic Signals in Large Language Model-based Student Assessment
stories.author: Dirk Hovy
bullet_points: The research investigates how student demographics influence the performance and output of Large Language Models (LLMs) used in educational assessment.
It addresses the dual challenge of using demographic data—it can be necessary for accessibility (e.g., readability) but also risks perpetuating bias and discrimination.
The study employs controlled prompting experiments to isolate and test the effects of explicit demographic signals within LLM-based evaluation systems.

stories.title: Building a Linux GPU Driver for the M4 Mac Mini in One Month
stories.author: ADevWithAnIdea
bullet_points: A project successfully built a Linux GPU driver for the M4 Mac Mini.
The development timeline was impressively short, completed in one month.
This demonstrates the feasibility of porting specialized hardware drivers to Linux.

stories.title: AI Wrote Half My Codebase. The Maintenance Bill Showed Up in Month Three.
stories.author: debashish_ghosal
bullet_points: The article discusses the initial appeal of using AI for rapid code generation.
It highlights a critical, often overlooked, long-term cost associated with AI-generated code (maintenance).
The narrative suggests that initial cost savings can be negated by unforeseen operational expenses.
